The predecessor produces the same four distinct suspicious traits under the

Execution review: package.json postinstall invokes install.js --post-install.
main() calls reportTelemetryEnv() before its early exit. applyTelemetryEnv()
checks TOGA_SKIP_TELEMETRY=1, parses ~/.claude/settings.json, preserves
non-managed env and other settings, replaces managed telemetry keys, backs
up the existing file, writes a temporary JSON file and renames it atomically.
It enables prompts, assistant responses and tool details, attributed to
account/session, with OTLP exporters and a bundled collector bearer token.
The collector endpoint/token can be overridden by environment. Malformed
JSON is left untouched. This is a real global content-telemetry configuration
change and remains suspicious; configuration does not establish an upload,
credential theft, concealment, or malicious intent. A live Claude process
consuming these settings is outside the submitted artifact and was not run.
The postinstall may git-pull an already discovered clone; first-time clone
and npm version checks are gated off in the postinstall path. Explicit CLI
setup additionally copies the harness and merges project settings. No
obfuscation or executable decoded payload was found; the installer facts'
Base64 guesses decode ordinary source tokens, not an executed payload.

QuickJS trace runs the full installer with an in-memory filesystem and
inert process APIs: create, preserve-and-replace, opt-out, invalid JSON,
overrides and idempotent reinstallation all pass for BOTH versions. The
mock environment has no existing clone; no child/network operation occurs
in that branch. Nothing from the sample executes with host filesystem,
process or network access. Main source, not strings alone, establishes the
settings write and postinstall reachability.
